---
title: Run a submission test
---

This step walks you through a complete test submission in the
[Slidetap](../../../services/slidetap.qmd) web UI:
log in, configure a project, upload your operator workbook, process the images,
curate any invalid items, and export a bundle to the outbox.

::: {.callout-important}
## Requires: stack running
The UI must be reachable before you begin. Complete
[Preflight + boot](boot.qmd) and confirm the login page opens at the address
`make up` printed.
:::

## Do a staging run first

**Run a complete test submission against the staging environment before you run
anything against production.** A staging run is a full rehearsal — the same test-run
steps, the same credentials mechanics, the same encrypt-and-upload — against an
environment where a mistake costs nothing. It is the cheapest way to surface a
missing `mappers.xlsx` row, a wrong `Image path`, or a storage-ownership problem
before it reaches the real archive.

These steps are written for staging by default: the credentials come from
[`login.staging.bp.nbis.se`](https://login.staging.bp.nbis.se/), and
[Upload to BigPicture](upload.qmd) sends the bundle to the staging inbox. Use
a small batch — a handful of slides is enough to exercise every step.

{{< include /datasets/submission/_staging-warning.qmd >}}

Switch only once a staging dataset has passed validation and uploaded cleanly;
the checklist is in [Prepare for production](prepare-for-production.qmd).

## 1. Log in

Open the UI address in your browser (e.g. **<https://localhost:443>**). You will
land on a **Login** page.

Enter the credentials you created in [TLS + credentials](tls-credentials.qmd):

- **User name** — the username from `make gen-credentials`
- **Password** — the password from `make gen-credentials`

Click **Login**. You will land on the **Projects** list.

<!-- TODO: screenshot — login page -->

## 2. Create a project

On the Projects list, click **New project**. The UI creates the project and
opens its **Settings** page immediately. A **Default** batch is created
automatically — you do not need to create one manually.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two separate pages, two separate UPDATE buttons

**Settings** and **Dataset** are two different pages in the Project sidebar,
each with its own **UPDATE** button. Filling in a field and clicking UPDATE
on one page does **not** save anything on the other — do both parts below,
in either order, and click UPDATE at the bottom of each page separately.
:::

**On the Settings page**

- **General** — set **Project Name** to something recognisable (e.g.
  `test-submission`).
- **Mapper groups** — this connects the project to the `mappers.xlsx`
  mappings you placed in [Reference data](reference-data.qmd).
- **Attributes** — the required fields (marked `*`) will already be filled
  in with test values. You can leave optional fields (Keywords, Geographical
  areas, Year of submission, etc.) blank for a test run.

Click **UPDATE** at the bottom of the Settings page.

**On the Dataset page**

Click **Dataset** in the Project sidebar (a separate page from Settings),
and check these fields:

- **Dataset Name** — a name for this dataset, distinct from the Project Name
  above. The **Project** and its **Dataset** are separate records that both
  start out called "New project"; renaming the project on the Settings page
  does *not* rename the dataset. Leave Dataset Name unset and every
  submission from this site exports under the same placeholder-derived
  bundle name, colliding with the last one. This field is what the export
  bundle directory and the identifier NBIS is notified about are derived
  from — see [Upload to BigPicture](upload.qmd) for the exact command
  syntax once you reach that step — so give it something that will still
  identify this submission uniquely later.
- **Metadata standard** — must be `3.0.0`, the default for a new project.
  Export refuses any other version, and [Validate the bundle](validate.qmd)
  fails a bundle that is not v3 on `METADATA_STANDARD`.
- **Description** — replace the placeholder text. Metadata v3 requires a
  description.
- **Node** — filled in from `BIGPICTURE_DEFAULT_NODE` (see
  [Configure](configure.qmd)). Change it only if this dataset belongs to
  another node.

Click **UPDATE** at the bottom of the Dataset page.

## 3. Upload the workbook

<!-- workaround: bigpicture-slidetap#56 (ID bullets). Remove when fixed. -->
::: {.callout-warning}
## Check your own workbook first: these mistakes give no error

- **Every ID cell is filled.** Blank IDs are merged into one item called `nan`.
- **Every `Image ID` and `Observation ID` is unique.** A repeated ID skips the
  whole row. A slide scanned twice needs two `Image ID`s.
- **Every slide has a staining.** Staining is mandatory.

After parsing, compare the item count on each **Curate** tab with your
workbook.
:::

In the left sidebar under **Batch**, click **Search**.

1. Click **Browse** and select `tests/data/metadata/metadata.xlsx` — the example
   workbook that ships with the pipeline. Ensure its **`Image path`** already
   points to the slide you placed in
   [Preflight + boot](boot.qmd#add-a-slide-image-for-the-test-run).
2. Click **Parse**.

The batch status changes to **Metadata Searching** while the pipeline reads the
workbook and creates items. When parsing finishes, the status becomes
**Metadata Search Complete** and the item list populates. You can also check the status under **Search**, where, after a refresh, the Status will read **Complete**.

## 4. Curate invalid items

Click **Curate** in the Batch sidebar. Items are listed by type across tabs
(e.g. *Sample*, *Image*).

An **invalid** item is one where a mapper could not resolve an attribute —
the value stays as typed but gets no coded value, the field shows
`No mapping for "<value>"`, and the item blocks the post-processing step
downstream. See
[mappers.xlsx](reference-data-mappers.qmd) for why this happens and how
to fix the mapping.

To fix an invalid item:

1. Click the row to open the detail panel. The unmapped attribute is shown in
   red.
2. Add the missing mapping row to `mappers.xlsx` in `PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR`
   and restart the stack (`make down`, then `make up`).
3. Select the affected items in the Curate table and click **Remap** to
   re-apply the updated mappers. No workbook re-upload is needed.

Make lasting fixes in `mappers.xlsx`, not in the curation UI. `make up`
re-applies the sheet: a changed key takes effect, and a mapping you edited in
the UI is reset to the sheet if the sheet has the same key.

For a test run with the provided example workbook, items should already be
valid if your `mappers.xlsx` covers the test values and the correct mapper group
is selected in Project Settings.

**Note:** WSIs will always be invalid at this stage; they can become valid after Pre-process.
<!-- TODO: screenshot — Curate tab showing an invalid item with attribute highlighted -->

::: {.callout-warning}
## Green in Curate is not proof the submission will export

A **valid** (green) item means a mapper resolved a value — not that the
value was actually saved. For an attribute nested inside another attribute
(a diagnosis or other pathology code inside an observation is the normal
case), **Remap** can compute the right value, mark the item valid, and still
never write that value to the database. Curate cannot show you this; the
item looks identical to one that is genuinely fine.

If **Remap** doesn't clear an invalid item after you've fixed its mapping
row, stop remapping it — that is the signature of a nested attribute, and
remapping again will keep reporting success without fixing anything.
Re-parse the workbook instead: see [Re-parse a workbook](#re-parse-a-workbook).

### Re-parse a workbook {#re-parse-a-workbook}

Re-parsing only re-creates items that no longer exist **anywhere in the
project**. Items with the same ID in another batch, or in the Default batch,
are reused as they are, without being mapped again.

- **Safe route:** create a new project and upload the full workbook there.
- **Faster route,** only if this batch shares no cases, specimens, blocks or
  slides with another batch: delete the batch, create a **New batch**, and
  upload the workbook into it.

Either way, compare the item count on each **Curate** tab before and after.
Fewer items means some were reused unchanged.

The only check that confirms the submission is actually intact is a
completed export (step 9): the project status reads **Export Complete**,
`METADATA/` inside the bundle holds XML files, and `IMAGES/` holds `.dcm`
files — see the Verify callout under step 9 for exactly where to look and a
caveat about `make export-check`. Treat every green status before that as
provisional — worth knowing now, before the image conversion in the next two
steps, rather than after.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Delete in Curate is final at the next Pre-process

**Delete** on an item only de-selects it, and can de-select related items with
it. **Pre-process** and **Post-process** then remove every de-selected item
for good, without a warning. Before you click either, check the deleted-items
view in **Curate** (the recycle icon) on every tab, and **Restore** anything
you still need.
:::

## 5. Pre-process images

Click **Pre-process** in the Batch sidebar. Click the **Pre-process** button.

The batch status changes to **Image Pre-processing** while the pipeline
downloads and DICOMizes the slide images. The table updates live — wait until
the status reaches **Image Pre-processing Complete**. 
Alternatively, watch in the Pre-process view to see all WSIs get status **Pre-Processed**.

If any image shows a failed status, click **Retry** next to it or select
multiple rows and use the bulk retry action.

## 6. Post-process images

Click **Post-process** in the Batch sidebar.

::: {.callout-important}
The **Start** button is only enabled when all items are valid. If it is greyed
out, return to **Curate** (step 4), resolve the remaining invalid items, and
come back.
:::

Click **Start**. The batch status changes to **Image Post-processing**, then
**Image Post-processing Complete**.

## 7. Verify (optional)

If the Batch sidebar shows **Verify**, use it to check a random sample of the
batch. If it doesn't, skip this step.

## 8. Lock the batch

Click **Lock** in the Batch sidebar, then click the **Lock** button. Every item
in the batch must be valid.

The batch status changes to **Curated and locked**. Once every batch is locked,
the project status changes to **Completed** and **Export** in the Project
sidebar becomes active.

To change a locked batch, click **Reopen** next to it in **Batches** (Project
sidebar). You can reopen a batch until its images are stored in step 9.

## 9. Export the bundle

Click **Export** in the Project sidebar (under **Project**, not **Batch**). The
page has two steps:

1. **Store images to outbox** — click **Store images**. Each batch shows its
   progress and ends as **Completed**. If storing stopped part-way, the button
   reads **Resume storing**.
2. **Export metadata** — once every batch is stored, click **Submit**.

::: {.callout-important}
## Storing images cannot be undone
After a batch's images are stored, the batch can no longer be reopened or
deleted. Check the batch before you click **Store images**.
:::

The project status changes to **Exporting**, then **Export Complete**. The
pipeline writes the export bundle to the outbox (`$PIPELINE_STORAGE/storage`).
<!-- workaround: slidetap#119. Remove when fixed. -->
If the status goes back to **Completed**, the export failed, even when the
**Tasks** page says *Succeeded*. Find the error with
`make logs s=slidetap-task`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `make export-check` currently reports FAIL on a good bundle

`make export-check` looks for `METADATA/` and `IMAGES/` directly inside the
project folder, but the pipeline actually writes them one level deeper,
inside a `DATASET_<alias>` subfolder. This is a known defect in the check
itself, not a sign your export failed. Until it's fixed, a `FAIL` from
`make export-check` is inconclusive — verify the bundle by hand instead, as
below.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Verify

You can still run `make export-check` as a quick first look:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows
In **Git Bash**, run:
```bash
make export-check
```
## macOS
```bash
make export-check
```
## Linux
```bash
make export-check
```
:::

But because of the defect above, confirm the bundle by hand: find the
project's folder under `$PIPELINE_STORAGE/storage` (named
&lt;project name&gt;.&lt;project uid&gt;), then check inside its `DATASET_<alias>`
subfolder:

- `METADATA/` should contain the required XML files (at minimum: `dataset.xml`,
  `image.xml`, `observation.xml`, `policy.xml`, `sample.xml`, `staining.xml`).
  Depending on your dataset, `observer.xml` and `annotation.xml` may also be present.
- `IMAGES/` should contain `.dcm` files.
- `LANDING_PAGE/` and `PRIVATE/` should also exist (a missing `landing_page.xml` is allowed; see [Validate the bundle](validate.qmd)).

The bundle is good when the project status reads **Export Complete** *and*
both folders above are populated — not when `make export-check` says so,
while this defect is open. Once confirmed, it is ready for
[Validate the bundle](validate.qmd).
:::

## 10. Prepare the landing page thumbnails

Slidetap writes a `THUMBNAILS/` folder inside the project directory. These are
local thumbnails only. The
submission bundle also needs a `LANDING_PAGE/THUMBNAILS/` folder inside
`DATASET_<alias>/` with the images you want to appear **publicly** in BigPicture.
This is a manual step — Slidetap does not populate it automatically.

::: {.callout-warning}
Everything under `LANDING_PAGE/` is world-visible after submission. Choose
representative images and avoid frames that carry sensitive information.
:::

## If something goes wrong

- **Parse produces no items.** The workbook format does not match the pipeline's
  expected structure. Check that you are uploading the correct `.xlsx` and that
  the sheet layout matches the import schema.
- **Images stay failed after retry.** Run `make logs` and check the image worker
  output. Common causes: slide files are not reachable at the path referenced in
  the workbook, or DICOM conversion failed on a specific file format.
- **Post-process Start button is greyed out.** One or more items are still
  invalid. Return to **Curate**, identify the invalid items, fix the mapping in
  `mappers.xlsx`, and remap.
- **Store images is greyed out on the Export page.** A batch is not locked yet;
  the page says how many. Lock each batch (step 8).
- **Submit is greyed out on the Export page.** The images of every batch are not
  stored yet. Hover over **Submit** for the reason, and finish **Store images**
  first (step 9).
- **Storing stopped with images not stored.** Retry the failed images, or take
  them out, on the batch's **Post-process** page. Then click **Resume storing**.
- **A project opens view-only.** It was created before the pipeline moved to
  metadata v3. To keep working on it, convert it: see
  [Converting projects to 3.0.0](https://github.com/imi-bigpicture/bigpicture-slidetap#converting-projects-to-300)
  in the bigpicture-slidetap README. A project that was already exported
  cannot be converted.
- **Export never reaches "Export Complete" — the project status just reverts to
  "Completed" with no visible error.** An observation is missing a required
  coded attribute (e.g. `diagnose`) that has no `"optional": true` flag in
  `model.json`. Check `make logs` for a `ValueError` naming the missing
  attribute's tag — export aborts at the *first* one it hits, so fixing one
  observation can just surface the next; expect a few rounds if several are
  affected. A green status in Curate doesn't rule this out — see the warning
  under step 4 (Curate) above. Specifically: if the missing attribute is
  nested inside another attribute (an observation's coded value, e.g.
  `diagnose`, is the normal case), **Remap will not fix it**, even though it
  reports success — re-parse the workbook instead (see
  [Re-parse a workbook](#re-parse-a-workbook)). For a plain, non-nested attribute, re-checking the
  mapping in `mappers.xlsx` and remapping does work. Either way, you can also
  mark the attribute optional in `model.json` instead of supplying a value —
  see [model.json](reference-data-model.qmd#required-and-optional-attributes).
  Editing `model.json` needs a stack restart — see [When do I need to
  restart?](boot.qmd#when-do-i-need-to-restart).
  <!-- workaround: bigpicture-slidetap#57. Remove when fixed. -->
  If the log says `Attribute <name> has no value` for a **Policy** or
  **Landing page** field, give that field a value on the Dataset page, click
  **UPDATE**, and submit again.
- **`export-check` reports `FAIL outbox not found`.** The `PIPELINE_STORAGE`
  path in `.env` does not exist or is not mounted correctly — see
  [Configure](configure.qmd).
- **`export-check` reports `FAIL no project directories`.** The export did not
  finish writing. Check `make logs` and confirm the project status shows
  **Export Complete** in the UI — if it instead shows **Completed**, see the
  missing-required-attribute entry above; that failure also prevents the
  bundle from being written.
